title: Linearized focusing and quantum entropy inequalities

items.title: Linearized future horizon focusing model
items.physical_scope: An adopted first-order Einstein-Hilbert semiclassical model on a fixed smooth four-manifold with a family of smooth time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metrics. Its background, state, and other inputs are restricted to the model-instance admissible domain below the supplied effective energy cutoff E_cut, which has dimension L^{-1} in the stated natural units. It has a stationary smooth null hypersurface, compact transverse cuts, an affinely normalized complete future generator flow, a supplied Hadamard state family, and one fixed stress prescription. Here “horizon” denotes only the supplied null hypersurface, not a causal or event horizon. It asserts no null energy condition, entropy inequality, solution existence, physical accuracy, or general higher-curvature focusing result.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the
curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ with
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$. Let $M$ be a fixed Hausdorff,
second-countable, oriented smooth four-manifold. For each dimensionless
$\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, supply a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g_\epsilon$ on $M$ with the stated signature and a time orientation (a chosen
future timelike cone). Each $(M,g_\epsilon)$ is globally hyperbolic: it is
strongly causal, meaning every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods that
each causal curve meets in a connected parameter interval, and each causal
diamond $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact. Here causal curves are piecewise
$C^1$ with consistently future- or past-directed causal tangent, and
$J^\pm(p)$ denote points reachable from or reaching $p$ by such curves.

For each $\epsilon$, let $H_\epsilon\subset M$ be a smooth embedded
three-dimensional submanifold whose induced metric has a one-dimensional
radical at every point. Its smooth nowhere-zero future null generator field
$k_\epsilon$ spans that radical and is affine,
$\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{k_\epsilon}k_\epsilon=0$. At $p\in H_\epsilon$ define
the screen space $\mathcal S_{\epsilon,p}:=k_\epsilon^\perp/\mathbb R
k_\epsilon$, where $k_\epsilon^\perp$ is taken in $T_pM$. Its positive screen
metric is $\bar g_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(X,Y)$, its screen deformation
form is
$$B_\epsilon([X],[Y]):=g_\epsilon(\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_Xk_\epsilon,Y),$$
and its expansion and shear are $\theta_\epsilon:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar
g_\epsilon}B_\epsilon$ and $\sigma_\epsilon:=B_\epsilon-\frac12\theta_\epsilon
\bar g_\epsilon$, respectively. These are the supplied smooth null-screen
conventions. The word “horizon” below denotes only $H_\epsilon$; no causal- or
event-horizon property is assumed.

Fix a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold $C$ and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\epsilon$, supply a smooth map
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$$
such that $\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$, and
every $\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ is an embedding with spacelike
image. The family supplies a fixed identification of generator labels and
affine normalization across $\epsilon$. With $[\lambda]=L$, this
parameterization gives $[k_\epsilon]=1$ in length coordinates.

Write $q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ for the
positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be
its Riemannian area density. On each finite parameter slab, the pulled-back
metric, area density, screen deformation form, expansion, and shear are jointly
$C^1$ in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$ and smooth in $y$; the underlying metric and
embedding family has the corresponding $\epsilon$-regularity and spatial
derivatives needed to define them. Call the reference geometry stationary in
this model when $B_0=0$ along every generator; then $\theta_0=\sigma_0=0$.
Define $\delta\theta:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon\right|_0$.

For each $\epsilon$, supply a positive normalized state $\omega_\epsilon$ on
the selected free scalar-field algebra. Its two-point distribution $W_\epsilon$
is a bisolution of the selected Klein–Gordon operator and has the supplied
Hadamard wavefront relation $\mathcal C^+_{g_\epsilon}$: pairs of future-null
covectors related by parallel propagation along a future-directed null
geodesic with common positive scale and opposite sign in the second slot,
including the coincident-point case. Supply a state-independent Hadamard
singular bidistribution
$H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ such that $W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is smooth, and one
fixed local stress prescription across the family,
$$T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}(x)=\lim_{x'\to x}D^{\epsilon}_{ab}(x,x')\bigl(W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}\bigr)(x,x')+C_{ab}[g_\epsilon;\mu,\mathbf c](x),$$
where $D^{\epsilon}_{ab}$ is the supplied finite-order bidifferential
operator and $C_{ab}$ the supplied state-independent local curvature
correction with the supplier's fixed positive renormalization scale $\mu$
($[\mu]=L^{-1}$ in these natural units) and finite renormalization conditions
$\mathbf c$. Thus the coincidence limit acts on a smooth difference, not on
the singular distributions separately. The family
$$F_\epsilon(\lambda,y):=(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\bigl(\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\bigr)$$
is jointly $C^1$ in $\epsilon$ and continuous in $(\lambda,y)$ on each finite
parameter slab. No independent graviton-fluctuation source is included.

Restrict every model input to the admissible domain supplied with its chosen
effective-model instance and to the regime below the supplier's positive energy
cutoff $E_{\mathrm{cut}}$. The supplier's SI cutoff is measured in joules; in
the natural units fixed here, $[E_{\mathrm{cut}}]=L^{-1}$. Neither the cutoff
value nor its admissible input domain is chosen here. Keep any prescribed
retarded data as supplied inputs, without
imposing a collapse geometry or scattering history. Select the
Einstein-Hilbert submodel by setting the supplier's curvature-squared couplings
to zero. Write $G_N$ for the supplier's Newton's constant $G$ in the natural-unit
convention $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, so $G_N>0$ has dimension $L^2$. Define
$$\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon F_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0.$$
Then $[\lambda]=L$, $[k_\epsilon]=1$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, and
$[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$.
Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, its tail is absolutely integrable on
each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ is the reference background area density.
Adopt, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the linearized focusing equation and
future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Terms quadratic in expansion or shear are omitted only at this first
perturbative order: both vanish in the stationary reference geometry and are
of order $\epsilon$ in the supplied family, so their squares are of order
$\epsilon^2$.
This postulate is an adopted model equation; it neither asserts that the model
describes nature nor identifies its null-stress moment with modular energy or
entropy.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete 44-page article; §2.2, equations (14)–(23), for the stationary-background first-order Raychaudhuri equation, affine future boundary condition, expansion/area relation and twice-integrated null-stress moment. The later modular/GSL bridge is not imported.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page lecture notes; §§4.6 and 4.8, especially equations (4.26)–(4.40), for affine null generators, screen expansion/shear and the exact null Raychaudhuri equation. The local model adopts only its stated first-order specialization.

items.title: Linearized horizon area difference is a weighted signed null-stress moment
items.physical_scope: A first-order geometric identity for a smooth compact cut of the stationary reference null hypersurface in the adopted Einstein-Hilbert model, with all model inputs in the supplied model-instance domain below E_cut (an energy cutoff of dimension L^{-1} in the stated natural units), a common differentiable metric and cut family, an affinely normalized future generator, a fixed future boundary condition, and an absolutely integrable stress moment. The result has no sign conclusion and makes no entropy, modular-Hamiltonian, QNEC, QFC, generalized-second-law, or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and
$[\lambda]=L$. Write $G_N$ for the Newton constant $G$ in the supplied
semiclassical equation after setting $c=\hbar=k_B=1$; then $G_N>0$ and
$[G_N]=L^2$. Take a model instance of the adopted Einstein-Hilbert focusing
postulate, with all its inputs restricted to the model-instance admissible
domain below the supplied effective energy cutoff $E_{\mathrm{cut}}$, whose
dimension in these natural units is $L^{-1}$. The numerical cutoff and
admissible domain are supplied with that instance.

Let $M$ be the common smooth four-manifold of the family of smooth
time-oriented Lorentzian metrics $g_\epsilon$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and
let $H_\epsilon\subset M$ be smooth embedded null hypersurfaces whose induced
metrics have one-dimensional radicals. Their smooth nowhere-zero future null
generator fields $k_\epsilon$ span those radicals and are affine,
$\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{k_\epsilon}k_\epsilon=0$. Use the postulate's global-hyperbolicity convention: strong causality, meaning
that every point has arbitrarily small neighborhoods met by each causal curve
in a connected parameter interval, and compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$.
Let $C$ be a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For dimensionless $\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, take the supplied
family
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon,\qquad \partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon,$$
with every $\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ an embedding with
spacelike image and with fixed generator labels and affine normalization
across $\epsilon$. The metric and embedding families have the postulate's
corresponding $\epsilon$-regularity on their common ambient manifold. The
pulled-back metric, area density, screen deformation form, expansion, and
shear are jointly $C^1$ in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$ and smooth in $y$ on each
finite parameter slab, with the spatial regularity needed to define them.

At $p\in H_\epsilon$, use the screen quotient
$\mathcal S_{\epsilon,p}=k_\epsilon^\perp/\mathbb Rk_\epsilon$ with positive
metric $\bar g_\epsilon([X],[Y])=g_\epsilon(X,Y)$. Its deformation form and
expansion are
$$B_\epsilon([X],[Y])=g_\epsilon(\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_Xk_\epsilon,Y),\qquad \theta_\epsilon=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g_\epsilon}B_\epsilon.$$
Assume the reference geometry is stationary in this model in the specified
sense $B_0=0$ along every generator, so $\theta_0$ and the shear
$\sigma_0=B_0-\frac12\theta_0\bar g_0$ vanish. Put
$$q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$$
for the positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let
$\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be its Riemannian area density. Define
$$A_\epsilon(\lambda):=\int_C\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda},\qquad \delta A(\lambda):=\left.\partial_\epsilon A_\epsilon(\lambda)\right|_0,\qquad dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}.$$

For each $\epsilon$, the supplied state $\omega_\epsilon$ is a positive
normalized linear functional; its two-point distribution $W_\epsilon$ is a
bisolution of the selected Klein-Gordon operator with Hadamard wavefront relation $\mathcal C^+_{g_\epsilon}$: its paired future-null covectors are related by parallel propagation along a future-directed null geodesic, with common positive scale and opposite sign in the second slot, including coincidence.
Use the postulate's single fixed local stress prescription
$$T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}(x)=\lim_{x'\to x}D^\epsilon_{ab}(x,x')\bigl(W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}\bigr)(x,x')+C_{ab}[g_\epsilon;\mu,\mathbf c](x),$$
where $W_\epsilon-H_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is smooth, $D^\epsilon_{ab}$ is the
supplied finite-order bidifferential operator, and $C_{ab}$ is the fixed
state-independent local curvature correction. Define
$$\delta\theta(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0,\qquad F_\epsilon(\lambda,y):=(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\bigl(\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\bigr),\qquad \delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon F_\epsilon(\lambda,y)\right|_0.$$
Assume $F_\epsilon$ has the postulate's joint $C^1$ dependence in $\epsilon$ and
continuous dependence on $(\lambda,y)$ on each finite parameter slab. Then $[k_\epsilon]=1$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, and
$[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$.

Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, has an absolutely integrable tail on
each generator, and satisfies the absolute first-moment bound
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty.$$
The postulate adopts, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the signed linearized
focusing equation and future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Then the finite limit $\delta A_\infty:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\delta A(R)$ exists
and, for every $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$,
$$\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)=8\pi G_N\int_C dA_0\int_\lambda^{\infty}(v-\lambda)\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv.$$
Consequently, if
$$M_\lambda:=\int_C dA_0\int_\lambda^{\infty}(v-\lambda)\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv,$$
then
$$\frac{\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)}{4G_N}=2\pi M_\lambda.$$
Here $[\delta A]=L^2$ and $M_\lambda$ is dimensionless. The quotient by
$4G_N$ is only a geometric normalization; it is not an entropy
identification.

title: Linearized focusing and quantum entropy inequalities — Examples

items.title: QNEC and QFC have different status and hypotheses
items.physical_scope: A source-scoped status distinction between selected quantum null energy inequalities and the quantum focusing conjecture. It establishes no entropy inequality, universal theorem, experimental result, or model applicability claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$. For each source formulation below,
supply its own Hausdorff, second-countable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ without
boundary, $d\ge2$, with a smooth symmetric nondegenerate metric $g$ of
signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$ and a smooth timelike field $T$ fixing the future
cone. A nonzero tangent vector $v$ is timelike, null or spacelike according
as $g(v,v)<0$, $=0$ or $>0$; it is causal in the first two cases and future
directed when $g(v,T)<0$. Use the metric-compatible torsion-free connection
$\nabla$, whose coordinate coefficients are
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ae}(\partial_b g_{ec}+\partial_c g_{eb}-\partial_e g_{bc})$,
with repeated indices summed from $0$ to $d-1$ and $(g^{ab})=(g_{ab})^{-1}$.
A causal curve is a continuous map from a real interval into $M$, locally
piecewise $C^1$, with nonzero consistently directed causal tangent on each
smooth piece. It is inextendible if its image admits no continuation as such
a curve at either end. A Cauchy surface here is a smooth embedded spacelike
hypersurface met in exactly one point by every inextendible causal curve;
spacelike means that the induced metric is positive definite. A smooth
embedded codimension-two cut splits such a surface when the complement is
the disjoint union of two open sides whose common boundary is the cut.
Supply a quantum-field state and its stress expectation $\langle T_{ab}\rangle$
on the modeled domain, with the source's renormalization and differentiability
conditions. These data describe the cited setups, independently of the
four-dimensional linearized horizon model.

For the cited quantum null energy condition (QNEC), let $\Sigma\subset M$
be such a cut and let $p\in\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal N$ be a smooth null
hypersurface orthogonal to $\Sigma$ near $p$, with smooth future-directed null
generators labelled by transverse coordinates $y$. On each generator use an
affine parameter $\lambda$ increasing toward the future with $[\lambda]=L$,
and normalize its tangent by $k^a=(d/d\lambda)^a$. Deforming $\Sigma$ to
$\Sigma[\lambda(y)]$ moves each generator by its indicated affine amount.
Restrict to a smooth embedded null hypersurface segment before generator
intersections: the radical
$L_p:=\{v\in T_p\mathcal N:g(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\in T_p\mathcal N\}$
is one-dimensional, is spanned by $k_p$, and $\nabla_k k=0$. For $d>2$, in transported cut coordinates put
$B_{AB}:=g(\nabla_{\partial_{y^A}}k,\partial_{y^B})$,
$\theta:=q^{AB}B_{AB}$ and $\sigma_{AB}:=B_{AB}-\theta q_{AB}/(d-2)$,
where $q$ is the induced positive cut metric. These define the classical
expansion and shear; there are no transverse expansion or shear components
when $d=2$. The source's
$S_{\mathrm{out}}[\lambda(y)]$ is the von Neumann entropy of the quantum-field
state restricted to one side of the deformed cut, equivalently to the
corresponding side of a Cauchy surface; the entropy itself may be divergent,
while the source-defined derivatives in the inequality are finite. With a
regulator admitting a positive trace-one reduced density operator $\rho$, the
von Neumann entropy is $-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$, with
$0\log0=0$; continuum entropy and its derivatives use the cited limiting
prescription, not an assumed finite unregulated density matrix. In §2,
equation (2.2), the authors call the pointwise formulation the “general
conjecture”; its local geometric condition is that the classical expansion
and shear vanish at $p$. For $d>2$ and a transverse patch of area $A$ about $p$,
$S_{\mathrm{out}}''(p)$ is the source-defined second affine variation for
that patch, with the other generators held fixed. The corresponding
pointwise formulation, in the small-area notation of equation (2.3), is
$$\langle T_{kk}(p)\rangle\ge\frac{1}{2\pi}\lim_{A\to0}\frac{S_{\mathrm{out}}''(p)}{A},\qquad \langle T_{kk}(p)\rangle:=\langle T_{ab}(p)k^ak^b\rangle.$$
Here $A$ is the geometric area of the transverse patch, computed from the
Riemannian metric induced on $\Sigma$, so $[A]=L^{d-2}$; both sides then have
dimension $L^{-d}$. Separately, the paper's abstract and
outline state applicability to free or superrenormalizable, massive or massless
bosonic fields on stationary null hypersurfaces, where “stationary” means that
the classical expansion vanishes everywhere. The authors explicitly treat the
QNEC proof as a fixed-background calculation without dynamical gravity. Its
§3.1–§4.5 argument treats $D>2$ on such a hypersurface. Section 5 derives the
free-scalar $D=2$ inequality
$\langle T_{2D}\rangle\ge(2\pi)^{-1}S''_{2D}$ by dimensional reduction
and strong subadditivity, with no shrinking transverse-area limit;
there $T_{2D}$ is the stress tensor of the reduced chiral scalar, whose action
on the reduced theory agrees with the transverse integral of $T_{kk}$, and
$S''_{2D}$ is the reduced entropy's second affine variation. Section 5 also
treats higher-spin bosonic fields and discusses extending the result to
superrenormalizable interactions conditionally on preservation of the
null-surface observable algebra and $T_{kk}$; the paper presents that
preservation as expected, not as established for arbitrary such interactions.
These source-reported scopes are distinct from the general pointwise
conjectural formulation of §2; they do not establish that formulation for every
field theory and background.

For the quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) in the cited semiclassical
Einstein-gravity formulation, use the geometry above and let $\sigma$ be a
smooth spacelike
codimension-two cut splitting a Cauchy surface, and let $\mathcal N$ be the
smooth null hypersurface generated by its orthogonal future-directed null
geodesics. Label the generators by local transverse coordinates
$y=(y^1,\ldots,y^{d-2})$ in $d$ spacetime dimensions. On each generator choose
an affine parameter $\lambda$ increasing to the future, with $\lambda=0$ at
$\sigma$, $[\lambda]=L$, and tangent $k=(d/d\lambda)$. A smooth
nonnegative function
$V(y)$ defines a cut $\sigma[V]$ by its intersection with generator $y$ at
$\lambda=V(y)$; restrict to profiles for which this is a well-defined smooth
cut that still splits a Cauchy surface. Let $q_{AB}[V]$ be the positive
induced metric on $\sigma[V]$ in the coordinates $y$, set
$h[V](y):=\det(q_{AB}[V](y))$, and define its area by
$$A[V]:=\int_{\sigma[V]}\sqrt{h[V](y)}\,d^{d-2}y.$$
For $d=2$, a cut is discrete, the empty metric determinant is $1$, and
this integral is counting measure; functional derivatives are derivatives
with respect to the individual cut-point displacements. The JT formulation
below uses a different gravitational entropy term and normalization.
Let $S_{\mathrm{out}}[V]$ be the von Neumann entropy of the quantum-field state
restricted to one side of $\sigma[V]$. It may be ultraviolet divergent by
itself. The cited source defines the generalized entropy by the following
combination and assumes its renormalized value is finite and cutoff-independent:
$$S_{\mathrm{gen}}[V]:=\frac{A[V]}{4G}+S_{\mathrm{out}}[V]+S_{\mathrm{ct}}[V],$$
where $S_{\mathrm{ct}}[V]$ is the source-prescribed local geometric
counterterm contribution; this is the source's $S_{\mathrm{grav}}[V]
=A[V]/(4G)+S_{\mathrm{ct}}[V]$ plus $S_{\mathrm{out}}[V]$, with
$\hbar=1$. In $d$ dimensions, $G>0$ has dimension $L^{d-2}$, so
$S_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is dimensionless. The source defines the quantum expansion
as the entropy response to a localized affine displacement, divided by the
geometric area of the transverse patch; in its functional-derivative
convention this is
$$\Theta[V;y_1]:=\frac{4G}{\sqrt{h[V](y_1)}}\frac{\delta S_{\mathrm{gen}}[V]}{\delta V(y_1)}.$$
For every admissible one-parameter family $V_\tau$ with
$\partial_\tau V_\tau(y)\ge0$, the QFC conjectures
$$\frac{\delta\Theta[V;y_1]}{\delta V(y_2)}\le0$$
for all generator labels $y_1,y_2$, with the coincident-point diagonal
understood in the source's distributional sense. This remains a conjecture in
general.

The cited 2017 Einstein-Hilbert-Gauss-Bonnet analysis constructs weak-curvature
QFC violations for $d\ge5$ at points where the null expansion and shear vanish.
The construction uses arbitrarily fine transverse localization. The authors'
v2 note reports that restricting entropy variations to surfaces smooth on the
scale associated with $G\gamma$ removes their violation, and leaves the
effective-field-theory-scale formulation as an open issue.

The cited 2026 v3 paper proves the restricted QFC (rQFC) for a class of
two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity models coupled to quantum field
theory, in regions where the total dilaton is positive and the matter state
satisfies the source's two-dimensional QNEC. The total dilaton is the smooth
scalar $\Phi=\phi_0+\phi:M\to\mathbb R$ of that two-dimensional model,
with constant $\phi_0$; it replaces transverse area in the entropy term.
For a moving cut point $P(\lambda)$ on a future affine null geodesic,
$\lambda\in I\subset\mathbb R$, keep the other cut points fixed and use
$S_{\mathrm{gen}}=\sum_i\Phi(P_i)/(4G)+S_{\mathrm{ren}}$, where
$S_{\mathrm{ren}}$ is the source-renormalized matter entropy. Here $G>0$
and $\Phi$ are dimensionless, and the source's quantum expansion is
$\Theta(\lambda)=4G\Phi(P(\lambda))^{-1}dS_{\mathrm{gen}}/d\lambda$,
with $\Phi(P(\lambda))>0$ and the derivatives assumed to exist. Its rQFC
asserts $d\Theta/d\lambda\le0$ where $\Theta=0$; this is weaker than
requiring that inequality at every cut. The authors also construct
full-QFC counterexamples in a JT regime where matter quantum effects compete
with the total dilaton. They state that this regime has no higher-dimensional
uplift; although the JT action has an approximate dimensional-reduction origin,
they treat this counterexample regime as an exact two-dimensional toy model
and caution that it is not strong evidence against the original QFC. These
theory- and regime-specific findings establish no universal QFC theorem for
arbitrary higher-curvature effective gravity. The linearized horizon model
discussed here defines no outside entropy, generalized-entropy functional, or
entropy shape derivative; it neither assumes nor derives QNEC or QFC.
